description: Temporal decoupling splits a simple temporal network (STN) that several agents share into one local network per agent, so that each agent can schedule and dispatch its own time points without talking to the others. Every time point except the common reference `z` belongs to one agent, and a constraint is shared when its endpoints belong to different agents. For each shared distance-graph edge `u → v` with weight `w`, the decoupling picks a value `c` and gives the owner of `u` the cut `t_u − z ≥ c` and the owner of `v` the cut `t_v − z ≤ c + w`. Together the two cuts imply the shared constraint, so any combination of locally consistent schedules is consistent with the whole plan. The cuts are chosen greedily, one shared edge at a time, on an incrementally maintained minimal network. Each `c` is the midpoint of the slack the edge still has, so both sides get half of it. Every choice keeps the network consistent, so the decoupling succeeds whenever the plan is consistent. It is a heuristic and does not maximise the total flexibility left to the agents, which would take a linear program.

papers.title: Algorithms for a Temporal Decoupling Problem in Multi-Agent Planning

papers.authors: James C. Boerkoel Jr., Edmund H. Durfee
papers.title: Distributed Reasoning for Multiagent Simple Temporal Problems
